findings.title: PhlimboV3 re-promoting a token with an outstanding bank silently re-arms emergencyTransfer over that bank, falsifying the :322-323 docblock's unconditional retired-bank carve-out
findings.rootCause: startPromotion (:356) rejects only address(0)/phUSD/rewardToken — it does NOT reject a token whose bank from an earlier promotion is still outstanding (totalUnclaimableOf[token] > 0). 'Retired' is a property of the SLOT, not of the BANK. Re-promoting silently makes an old bank LIVE again, so :335-340 sweeps its entire balance. The unclaimablePromoOf LIABILITY survives with no assets behind it and the user's claimUnclaimablePromo reverts.
findings.specConflict: PhlimboV3.sol:322-323 states UNCONDITIONALLY: 'A RETIRED token's bank (promoToken == address(0) for it) is unreachable here and stays pullable via claimUnclaimablePromo.' Only true while the token is not re-promoted. The docblock's own parenthetical reveals the mechanism but the prose does not draw the conclusion.
findings.lawBasis: Law 3 footgun with a NON-OBVIOUS consequence. Surprise test MET: a competent, non-malicious owner reading :322-323 would not expect a routine second campaign with the same partner token (step 3) to re-arm the sweep (step 4).
findings.impact: Bounded and already inside an accepted trade-off envelope — emergencyTransfer ALREADY sweeps the LIVE token's bank as an explicitly documented, accepted trade-off with out-of-band remediation (:316-323). The incremental harm is that a previously-carved-out RETIRED bank silently loses its carve-out. No new value is exposed beyond what the escape hatch already claims; what breaks is the ACCURACY of the carve-out the docblock advertises.

poc.result: PASS. Asserts BOTH directions: while retired the bank survives emergencyTransfer exactly as documented; after re-promotion the same call sweeps it to zero, the liability record stays intact, and the user's pull reverts.

findings.recommendation: Documentation-first, per the standing ejector-seat precedent. (a) amend the :322-323 docblock to state the carve-out holds only while the token is not re-promoted; (b) if a stronger guarantee is wanted, have startPromotion emit a warning event (or require an explicit acknowledgement argument) when totalUnclaimableOf[token] > 0; (c) accept as-is and document.

findings.title: FAITHFULNESS: story-027's NEW retired-token solvency invariant (SolvencyDetermination.md §4) does not survive an emergencyTransfer — permanently false for that token, plus a phantom-reserve strand on re-use
findings.rootCause: emergencyTransfer (:328-340) sweeps the live promo token's ENTIRE balance — bank included, by design — but does NOT clear unclaimablePromoOf / totalUnclaimableOf. The bank becomes a pure liability record with no backing. The token then RETIRES, at which point the doc's 'live token only' carve-out no longer applies and the invariant is permanently false: totalUnclaimableOf[t] > 0 == t.balanceOf(phlimbo). The published step-5 solvency procedure then reports the contract insolvent for t, FOREVER.
findings.specText: SolvencyDetermination.md §4, ADDED IN THIS RANGE by story-027 (commit 1c4e1a9): 'A separate invariant holds for every token t ever used as a promo token, including retired ones: t.balanceOf(phlimbo) >= totalUnclaimableOf[t] ... (emergencyTransfer is the owner-gated exception for the *live* token only — a retired token's bank is out of its reach.)' Restated as step 5 of the public solvency procedure.
findings.deviation: The invariant is stated to hold for EVERY token ever promoted, including retired ones. It does not survive an emergencyTransfer that fires while a bank is live. The doc's parenthetical acknowledges the live-token sweep as an 'exception' but does not carry that exception into the RETIRED state, where it in fact lands.
findings.secondOrderEffect: PHANTOM RESERVE. Because the stale bank is never cleared, if t is later re-used as the promo token, finalizePromotion:517-519 computes `leftover = balance - banked` against the PHANTOM banked amount, permanently stranding that much of the NEW promotion's genuine leftover (the slot is zeroed at :521-523, so the only exits left are another promotion in t or another emergencyTransfer). The saturating subtraction prevents a REVERT but not the STRAND.

dropped.reason: TASKED RESOLUTION. All four are Aderyn 'Reentrancy: State change after external call' on the FoT balance-delta guards in startPromotion (:364/:366) and topUpPromotion (:389/:391). VERIFIED AGAINST SOURCE by the deduplicator: the flagged 'external call' is `IERC20(token).balanceOf(address(this))` — a VIEW. A staticcall-shaped balance read cannot mutate state or hand control flow to an attacker, so there is no reentrancy semantics to violate; the 'state change after' is the intended `promoToken = ...; promoRewardBalance = ...` assignment that MUST follow the funding transfer. Both functions are onlyOwner. UNCORROBORATED by Slither (which independently found no reentrancy here) and Aderyn's own confidence is 'medium'. Moreover the balance-delta form these lines implement is not merely harmless but LOad-BEARING: econ-scanner's R-2 shows the balanceBefore-delta check at :364-366 is exactly what makes retired-bank re-promotion arithmetic self-consistent — 'a naive balanceOf == amount check would have broken here'. Dropping a correctness-critical guard as a reentrancy bug would be actively harmful.
